attributes.title: tag_move
attributes.description: Move Tags and Folders to a new parent via system.tag.move with the handler-fixed Abort collision policy, with the D30 2 Tag config fingerprint as the per-target Precondition token. Each item carries a source path, the exact destination path the node must land on, and the tcf1 fingerprint of the source's own tag_get_config read. This Tool is CONFIG and destructive: the source is gone from where it was. Reads the Runtime Target Policy first and fails closed with operation_disabled when it is missing or unusable. D30 6 checks both ends: the source and the destination are measured against the tag_move Target allowlist (a UDT definition only under an explicit _types_ entry), and owner ruling 1 refuses either end inside the reserved IgnitionMCPPolicy provider with permission_denied whatever the allowlist says, including an explicit *, before the allowlist is consulted. The destination's last segment must equal the source's, because one system.tag.move call moves a path list into one destination folder under each source's own name; a move that renames is tag_rename's. Preflight validates every item's input, both Targets, the source's existence and fingerprint, and the destination's absence before any item executes: a stale fingerprint is conflict, a source that is not there is not_found, and an occupied destination is conflict, so nothing is ever overwritten. After Preflight the items execute one at a time with no rollback and the Native QualityCode of each system.tag.move call is that item's outcome; a destination that appears between the fingerprints and the dispatch aborts that item - conflict, never a success. Observed state is the destination present and the source absent. Runtime audit follows the policy's auditMode; a failed post-Mutation audit write gives auditRecorded=false, never a failure. Every request is bounded (D10): 20 targets by default up to the 100-target hard maximum, and the deployment may raise the default through tagMoveMaxItems in the Runtime Target Policy; both paths in an item and the batch as a whole have finite ceilings, and an over-budget request is a limit_exceeded refusal before any native call. A refused Target or Precondition writes one Runtime audit decision row (none in off mode, fail-closed in required mode).

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: 1..100 move items: {"sourcePath": provider-qualified Tag or Folder path to move, "destinationPath": the exact new path, whose last segment must equal the source's, "expectedFingerprint": the tcf1 fingerprint from tag_get_config for the source path}. The source must exist with that fingerprint and the destination must not exist, or the whole batch is refused before anything moves. Default 20 (D10), hard maximum 100.
